editorial:
Ever wonder how Sherlock Holmes first crossed paths with his biggest enemy? You get to see that origin story here. Instead of the older, polished detective you might know, you meet a younger Sherlock who is still figuring things out. He is brilliant but a bit rough around the edges, and the vibe feels like a gritty street fight rather than a fancy parlor game. You will follow him as he tries to stop Professor Moriarty from taking over the heroin trade in London. It is a cool way to see the start of a legendary rivalry while exploring the dark side of the city.

The acting is solid, and the tension keeps you leaning in, though the pacing slows down a bit in the middle. If you love a good cat-and-mouse game, you will really enjoy how these two geniuses try to outsmart each other. It is a great pick for a rainy weekend. To get the best experience, you should try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for those sharp visuals. If you prefer owning your movies, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go for the best quality.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head when Sherlock finally corners Moriarty. After a series of clever traps, Sherlock manages to expose the Professor's drug ring and stop his plan to control the city. They do not have a final fight to the death like in other versions, but it sets up their lifelong hatred. You see that while Sherlock wins this round, Moriarty is still a dangerous threat who will haunt him for years to come.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves origin stories and clever mysteries.
